title: Amped 3
subtitle: A snowboarding trip takes a strange turn

body: Amped 3 is Indie Built's Xbox 360 snowboarding game, released in North America on 22 November 2005. It follows a group of riders through a deliberately eccentric story while allowing the player to explore several mountain resorts. Challenges scattered across the slopes provide ways to earn money, respect and new equipment. The boarding remains the centre of the experience, but its presentation moves away from a restrained sporting tone. Hand puppets, animation and other visual styles turn the scenes between runs into unexpected changes of mood and medium.

Some challenges ask for particular tricks, while others involve racing, collecting objects or matching a professional rider. Sleds and snowmobiles provide further variations. Respect unlocks new mountain areas and advances the story, making optional-looking activities part of the route through the campaign. The player can choose a nearby challenge that suits the available terrain or return to improve an earlier performance. Progress therefore grows from repeated use of the resorts, as a familiar slope becomes a place to attempt a different trick, earn another reward or reach the next opening.

The third and final Amped game was published by 2K after the earlier Xbox entries. Its unusual story follows a disputed holiday fund and a cast whose problems quickly become more extravagant than a conventional snowboarding competition. Two-player minigames offer local diversions, while online features focused on a high-score leaderboard rather than shared riding. Amped 3's character comes from the contrast between traversable mountain spaces and scenes that refuse to keep one visual style. It treats the snowboarding trip as the foundation for a much stranger comedy about the people taking it.
